title: Terremoto de Neiva de 1967.
text: El jueves 9 de febrero de 1967, a las 10:24 de la mañana, un violento sismo de magnitud 7.2 Mw y profundidad superficial se registró en el departamento del Huila (Colombia). Los departamentos más afectados fueron Huila, Caquetá y Tolima, donde se presentaron colapsos y daños severos en construcciones.

title: 3 de marzo :Las FARC realizan la Emboscada de La Perdiz en Algeciras (Huila), dejando 16 militares muertos.
text: La emboscada de La Perdiz fue el segundo ataque de importancia lanzado por las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia contra el Ejército Nacional de Colombia. El ataque ocurrió 3 de marzo de 1967, en la vía que de Santana Ramos conduce a Algeciras, Huila.

title: Creado el Canal RCN como productora de televisión.
text: Canal RCN, también conocido como RCN Televisión o simplemente RCN, es un canal de televisión abierta colombiano, propiedad de la Organización Ardila Lülle. Fue fundado como empresa productora de contenido televisivo el 23 de marzo de 1967 e inició sus emisiones como canal independiente el 10 de julio de 1998.

title: Vuelta a Colombia 1967 ganada por Martín Emilio Cochise Rodríguez.
text: Martín Emilio Rodríguez Gutiérrez, más conocido como "Cochise" Rodríguez, es un exciclista colombiano que compitió en las décadas de 1960, 1970 y principios de 1980, destacándose tanto en ruta como en pista. Fue poseedor del récord mundial de la hora, establecido en el velódromo Agustín Melgar de la Ciudad de México en 1970.

title: Inaugurado el Teatro Pablo Tobón Uribe de Medellín
text: El Teatro Pablo Tobón Uribe es una sala de teatro de Medellín, Colombia, ubicado en la avenida La Playa. Ha sido uno de los más tradicionales escenarios de la ciudad, ofrece una variada programación durante todo el año, fue inaugurado el 2 de agosto de 1967, y es el que mejor acústica ofrece para presentaciones musicales y teatrales.

title: Incidentes del Douglas DC-4 de Aerocóndor Colombia en 1967
text: Los incidentes de los dos Douglas DC-4 de Aerocóndor Colombia hace referencia a dos incidentes sufridos con matrícula HK-757, en los cuales se detonó una bomba a bordo y se secuestró el vuelo.
wiki: Incidentes del Douglas DC-4 de Aerocóndor Colombia en 1967

title: publicada la Novela Cien años de soledad de Gabriel García Márquez
text: Cien años de soledad es una novela del escritor colombiano ganador del Premio Nobel de Literatura Gabriel García Márquez. Es opinión general que se trata de una obra maestra de la literatura hispanoamericana y universal, y es una de las obras más traducidas y leídas en español.​ En marzo de 2007, el IV Congreso Internacional de la Lengua Española celebrado en Cartagena de Indias la consideró una de las obras más i…

title: Envenenamiento en Chiquinquirá (Boyacá), 800 personas consumieron pan envenenado y 78 murieron.
text: El envenenamiento en Chiquinquirá se refiere a un incidente ocurrido el sábado 25 de noviembre de 1967 en el municipio de Chiquinquirá, departamento de Boyacá, Colombia, cuando al menos 78 personas, en su mayoría niños, murieron, y alrededor de 800 resultaron intoxicadas tras desayunar pan contaminado con Folidol, un potente y tóxico plaguicida.​​

title: Aparecen Espectaculares JES de musicales en televisión.
text: Espectaculares JES fue uno de los programas musicales más importantes de la televisión colombiana creado, dirigido y presentado por Julio Sánchez Vanegas emitido desde 1967 hasta 1994. También fue el primer programa en viajar por todo el mundo conociendo a los cantantes internacionales.

title: Inaugurado el Puente Internacional José Antonio Páez en Arauca que comunica a Colombia y Venezuela.
text: El Puente Internacional José Antonio Páez es un cruce limítrofe sobre el río Arauca que comunica las poblaciones de El Amparo en Venezuela, y Arauca en Colombia.

title: Fundado el Ejército Popular de Liberación (Colombia).
text: El Ejército Popular de Liberación, llamados por el gobierno de Colombia como Los Pelusos, fue una organización guerrillera insurgente colombiana de extrema izquierda fundada en 1967, basada en los principios e ideologías del marxismo-leninismo y que formaba parte del conflicto armado interno de Colombia. El EPL ya se desmovilizo siendo el ELN la única guerrilla activa de Colombia.​ Cerca de 2200 integrantes del EP…

title: Astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White, and Roger B. Chaffee are killed in a fire during a plugs-out test for Apollo 1.
text: Virgil Ivan "Gus" Grissom was an American astronaut, and one of the original Mercury Seven selected by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) for Project Mercury, a program to train and launch astronauts into outer space. Grissom went on to be a Project Gemini and Apollo program astronaut for NASA. As a member of the NASA Astronaut Corps, Grissom was the second American to fly in space in 1961.

title: The United States, Soviet Union and UK sign the Outer Space Treaty.
text: The Outer Space Treaty, formally called the Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies, is a multilateral treaty that forms the basis of international space law. Negotiated and drafted under the auspices of the United Nations, it was opened for signature in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Uni…

title: Surveyor 3 probe lands on the Moon.
text: Surveyor 3 is the third lander of the American uncrewed Surveyor program sent to explore the surface of the Moon in 1967 and the second to successfully land. It was the first mission to carry a surface-soil sampling-scoop.

title: Soviet cosmonaut Vladimir Komarov is killed during the landing of Soyuz 1.
text: An astronaut, meaning 'star', and ναύτης (nautes), meaning 'sailor') is a person trained, equipped, and deployed by a human spaceflight program to serve as a commander or crew member of a spacecraft. Although generally reserved for professional space travelers, the term is sometimes applied to anyone who travels into space, including scientists, politicians, journalists, and space tourists.

title: The Soviet Venera 4 probe descends through the Venusian atmosphere, which it analyzes.
text: Venera 4, also designated 4V-1 No.310, was a probe in the Soviet Venera program for the exploration of Venus. The probe comprised a lander, designed to enter the Venusian atmosphere and parachute to the surface, and a carrier/flyby spacecraft, which carried the lander to Venus and served as a communications relay for it.

title: Mariner 5 probe flies by Venus.
text: Mariner 5 was a spacecraft of the Mariner program that carried a complement of experiments to probe Venus's atmosphere by radio occultation, measure the hydrogen Lyman-alpha (hard ultraviolet) spectrum, and sample the solar particles and magnetic field fluctuations above the planet. Its goals were to measure interplanetary and Venusian magnetic fields, charged particles, plasma, radio refractivity and UV emissions…

title: Apollo program: NASA launches a Saturn V rocket carrying the unmanned Apollo 4 test spacecraft from Cape Kennedy.
text: The Saturn V is a retired American super heavy-lift launch vehicle developed by NASA under the Apollo program for human exploration of the Moon. The rocket was human-rated, had three stages, and was liquid-fueled.

title: Pulsars discovered by Jocelyn Bell Burnell working with Antony Hewish at the University of Cambridge, for which Hewish is awarded a Nobel Prize in Physics in 1974. These rapidly pulsating radio sources are explained a year later as…
text: A pulsar is a highly magnetized rotating neutron star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles. This radiation can be observed only when a beam of emission is pointing toward Earth (similar to the way a lighthouse can be seen only when the light is pointed in the direction of an observer), and is responsible for the pulsed appearance of emission.

title: Dedication of Liverpool Metropolitan Cathedral in England, designed by Frederick Gibberd, with stained glass by John Piper, Patrick Reyntiens and Margaret Traherne and a bronze crucifix by Elisabeth Frink.
text: Liverpool Metropolitan Cathedral, officially known as the Metropolitan Cathedral of Christ the King and locally nicknamed "Paddy's Wigwam" or "The Mersey Funnel", is the seat of the Archbishop of Liverpool and the mother church of the Archdiocese of Liverpool in Liverpool, England. The Grade I Metropolitan Cathedral is one of Liverpool's many listed buildings.

title: Gilbert and George first meet while studying sculpture at St Martins School of Art in London.
text: Gilbert Prousch, sometimes referred to as Gilbert Proesch, and George Passmore (born 8 January 1942) are artists who work together as the collaborative art duo Gilbert & George. They are known for their formal appearance and manner in performance art, and for their brightly coloured graphic-style photo-based artworks.

title: 1967 Basel Picasso paintings purchase referendum: The people of Basel (Switzerland) vote to purchase two paintings by Picasso to retain them in the Kunstmuseum Basel.
text: Pablo Ruiz Picasso was a Spanish painter and sculptor who spent most of his adult life in France. One of the most influential artists of the 20th century, he is known for co-founding the Cubist movement, the invention of constructed sculpture, the co-invention of collage, and for the wide variety of styles that he helped develop and explore.

title: John Willett publishes Art in a City, a pioneering sociological study of art in a single city, Liverpool.
text: John William Mills Willett, MBE was a British translator and scholar, who is remembered for translating the work of Bertolt Brecht into English.

title: Foundation of the Project Arts Centre, Dublin.
text: Project Arts Centre is a multidisciplinary arts centre based in Temple Bar, Dublin, which hosts visual arts, theatre, dance, music, and performance.
